content.readme:
net-merge

Use all your internet connections at the same time.
Combine Wi-Fi, Ethernet and phone hotspots, so downloads, games and browsers get the speed of every connection added up.

Website · Download · Android · Install · Add a second connection · Troubleshooting · How it works


A Mac with Wi-Fi + an Android phone. The menu shows both connections working at once. Watch the full 45-second video.

net-merge uses all your network adapters together. It works on **Windows, macOS and Linux**. It is free. There is no account, no server and no VPN. A real test with Wi-Fi + an Android USB tether + an iPhone hotspot, 9 downloads at once: **232-303 Mbit/s**. The fastest connection alone gave about 121 Mbit/s. | Windows: hover the icon | Windows: the menu | macOS: the menu bar | |---|---|---| | ![Tooltip: Merging, speed of each adapter and the total](docs/tray-tooltip.png) | ![Menu: total, each adapter's speed and flows, IPv6 option, Pause merging, Quit](docs/tray-menu.png) | ![macOS menu: total 399 Mbit/s, en0 and feth0 each with their flows, Pause merging, Quit](docs/tray-menu-macos.png) | ## How it helps net-merge gives every new connection to one of your links. When an app opens many connections, they spread over all your links. - **Good for:** Steam and game downloads, browsers, system updates, cloud uploads (Google Drive), download managers like IDM, torrents. - **Not for:** one single connection. One connection always uses one link, so one big file from one connection does not get faster. Browsers can split a download into several connections; see the tip under [Use it](#use-it). - **Works for every app**, TCP and UDP, IPv4 and IPv6. You do not set up a proxy. - **Smart:** faster links get more connections. A link with no internet gets none until it works again. - **Safe:** if net-merge crashes, your internet keeps working. - **Light:** about 0.18 CPU cores per 100 Mbit/s. ## Install **macOS and Linux**: paste this into a terminal. ``` curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/net-merge/net-merge/main/install.sh | sh ``` **Windows**: paste this into PowerShell. ``` irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/net-merge/net-merge/main/install.ps1 | iex ``` Antivirus blocked it? content.readme:
Your company's data, connected into one ontology.

Helix Cloud · Docs · Run it on your computer · Apache 2.0

Connect your databases, tools and documents, let an agent draft an ontology over them, and load it into [HelixDB](https://docs.helix-db.com) as one connected graph. Explore it, follow every value back to the row or quote it came from, and ask questions with cited answers. Use it hosted at [foundry.helix-db.com](https://foundry.helix-db.com), or run it on your own computer with one command.

## Get started with your coding agent **On Helix Cloud.** Open [foundry.helix-db.com](https://foundry.helix-db.com) and click **Set up with your agent**. It copies a prompt for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or any agent that can run commands. The agent adds the Helix MCP, signs you up through it if you don't have an account yet, and builds your first ontology with you. You never need the Helix dashboard: the agent sends you a link only to sign in or to enter a password or key. **On your computer.** With [Docker](https://docs.docker.com/get-started/get-docker/) running, paste this into your agent: ```text Set up Helix Foundry on this computer. Clone https://github.com/helixdb/helix-foundry.git (or use the copy I already have), then follow its README.md and local/README.md to start it with Docker Compose and check that it is up. Ask me before deleting data, removing Docker volumes or stopping anything that is already running. When it is ready, give me the URL and tell me what to do next. ``` Approve its `git` and `docker` commands one at a time rather than all `docker` commands up front. You enter API keys and database passwords in Foundry, in your browser: your agent never needs them. ## Run it on your computer You need Docker with Compose v2, ports 3000 and 8333 free, and room for a few GB of images on the first start. ```sh git clone https://github.com/helixdb/helix-foundry.git cd helix-foundry docker compose up -d --wait ``` Open **http://localhost:3000**. There is no account and nothing to set up: one owner, every connector and feature on, and **My workspace** to start in. **AI** runs where Foundry finds it: Claude or OpenAI when the shell you ran `docker compose up` from has an `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or `OPENAI_API_KEY`, else a model that calls tools in Ollama (`docker compose --profile ollama up -d` runs one beside Foundry, or use Ollama on your computer), else LM Studio on your computer. **Settings › AI models** says which it chose and why, and switches to Ollama, Claude, OpenAI, Azure OpenAI or Amazon Bedrock with your own key, or any OpenAI-compatible server (vLLM, a gateway). [local/README.md](local/README.md) covers what runs, where data lives, each AI provider, Ollama in Docker, ports, and how to reach databases on this machine. **What you do next** 1. No data to hand? Click **Use the sample**: Acme Corp, a made-up software company, as a PostgreSQL database (customers, subscriptions, invoices, support tickets, usage) and documents (contracts, call notes, an incident report). It walks you through the data, the goal, a ready-made ontology, its load and a question, in about a minute, once Foundry has an AI provider. 2. Otherwise, connect your data or upload documents, say what you want to know, and let the ontology agent draft the ontology. 3. Review the draft, make it current and load it into HelixDB. 4. Explore the graph and its records, or ask the **Analyst**.

## What you get - **Connectors** for PostgreSQL, MySQL, Amazon S3, Stripe, PostHog, WorkOS, GitHub, Linear, Granola, Cal.com, Slack, Notion and Google Workspace, documents (Markdown, text, PDF) and table files (CSV, TSV, JSON, JSON Lines, Parquet). On Helix Cloud, API sources also take records your apps and agents send. - **Syncs that read only what changed:** PostgreSQL and MySQL change capture where the database allows it, and incremental reads from every other connector. - **An ontology agent** that drafts types, links, rules, and the tables and documents each comes from, from your data and your goal. You review it, edit it and make a version current

# ARTEX AI autonomous penetration testing system. Multi-agent LLM, Go backend, Next.js frontend. AI 自主渗透测试系统（Go 后端 + Next.js 前端）。 [![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/trhhubsd/ARTEX)](https://github.com/trhhubsd/ARTEX/releases) [![License: AGPL-3.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-AGPL--3.0-blue)](LICENSE)
ARTEX is a multi-agent system for autonomous penetration testing in an isolated lab: a planner and workers share an asset graph and an exploration graph, with human-in-the-loop approval and full traffic recording. content.readme:
Git designed for AI agents.

Anthropic built **Scion**, a faster version control system for coding agents, and described it in [Redesigning source control](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/redesigning-source-control): a server-centric system built for hundreds of agents that read, write and land code at the same time. Scion is internal to Anthropic and is not available to the public. So I built **gitai**: an open-source version of that design that anyone can run, and that the community can improve and maintain together. MIT licensed. Vendor neutral: the server never calls a language model, and every AI feature works with any provider, or none. gitai is an independent implementation of the publicly described design. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by Anthropic. --- ## Why Classic Git hosting was built for humans who clone a repository, work for hours and push once. Coding agents work differently: thousands of short-lived tasks, each touching a few files, each wanting to land in seconds, all on the same branches. Full clones, merge queues and client-side history walks become the bottleneck. Scion's answer is to move the work to the server: clients stay online and fetch only what they need, history questions are answered (and cached) by the server, changes land through a compare-and-swap instead of a queue, every update is an entry in a changeset log, and the repository state lives in a consistent database plus object storage so servers scale out. gitai implements these ideas, with normal Git repositories underneath. ## The Scion ideas, implemented | Scion idea | In gitai | |---|---| | **Always-online clients** that fetch exactly what they need | `ObjectService` serves single objects and sparse trees; `graft clone` and `graft sparse` materialize only the paths you ask for. | | **Source control as an API**: history runs on the server | Blame, path history, ancestry and code search run server-side and are memoized as derived data, computed once per commit. | | **Landing without a merge queue** | `UserLand` rebases a change onto the current tip and lands it with a compare-and-swap; concurrent lands on one branch are batched into a single reference update. | | **Automatic conflict resolution** | A conflicting land is resolved by a resolver you choose (any LLM provider, a deterministic tool, or none) through a versioned, vendor-neutral protocol. A model's resolution is only a proposal: it lands by itself only if the `verify.command` you configure passes on the exact tree that would land, and otherwise the agent gets the conflict package with the proposal. The deterministic rules you configure need no such condition of their own, and are verified on the exact tree as well when you turn the verification on (`verify.enabled`). | | **Changeset log** | Every accepted reference update is recorded with its operation and actor in a dense, ordered log that clients list or watch live. | | **Storage core: a database and object storage, stateless servers** | Each change is a changeset in a write-ahead log in SQLite or PostgreSQL, with a compare-and-swap per reference; packs live in object storage (file, S3, GCS, Azure). Server nodes are caches that any node can rebuild, so you add nodes to scale. | | **Test after landing, revert the culprit** | `graft-verify` tests the tip, bisects a failure and reverts the change that broke it. | | **Monitoring agents ("superfans")** | Agents follow the changeset stream and report what matters to each component, also through Slack. | | **Agent-friendly review** | Reviews with semantic approval rules: a comment-only change can need fewer approvals than a logic change. | | **Agents as first-class users** | Per-agent tokens, an RPC allowlist and branch policies decide what each agent may do. | | **Strict cache tiers** | `graft-cache` caches immutable objects in daemon and regional tiers, verifying every object. | ## Architecture ``` agents, CI jobs, sparse workspaces graft CLI / Go SDK | v gRPC +-------------------------------------------------+ | graft-cache (optional daemon and cache tiers) | +----------------

content.readme:
# UnfairPlay

UnfairPlay recovers a FairPlay model from an enrolled Mac and uses it to
decrypt personalized iOS IPAs. It is a standalone Go program.

It does not log in to Apple, buy apps, or download IPAs. You can use ipatool or
another downloader for that part.

## Legal and ethical use

Use UnfairPlay only with apps you lawfully acquired and accounts and devices
you control. It is intended for interoperability, preservation, and authorized
research. The authors do not condone piracy, credential theft, copyright
infringement, or unauthorized distribution of decrypted apps.

## Discord

Project discussion and support: [UnfairPlay Discord](https://discord.gg/hpwvuQHfaf).

## Build

```sh
go build -o unfairplay ./cmd/unfairplay
```

## Usage

First, sign in to the native Mac App Store. Install an iPhone or iPad app and
open it once. Download a matching encrypted IPA with the same Apple Account.

Set up reusable decryption once:

```sh
sudo ./unfairplay setup \
  --app /Applications/App.app \
  --ipa App.ipa
```

Large enrollment databases print bounded recovery progress to standard error.
The final JSON result remains on standard output.

The setup result includes `plaintext_verified` for the matching IPA. A successful
setup can report `false` when any decrypted image lacks pre-encryption hashes;
this is separate from whether the model was recovered and saved successfully.

The saved model is private. It is tied to the Mac App Store enrollment, not to
one app, so it can decrypt other personalized IPAs from the same enrollment.
Back it up only in encrypted storage and never share it.

Decrypt another IPA:

```sh
./unfairplay decrypt --input AnotherApp.ipa
```

The default model directory is inside the user configuration directory. Set
`UNFAIRPLAY_MODEL_DIR` or pass `--model` to use another location.

IPAs with extensions and watch apps are decrypted in one pass.

The output keeps the input's `SC_Info` licenses and `iTunesMetadata.plist`,
which identify the Store account. To create a redacted copy for private
analysis or authorized collaboration, add `--strip-account-data`: it omits
every `SC_Info` member and removes the Apple ID and purchaser fields from
`iTunesMetadata.plist`. Redaction does not authorize redistributing the app;
the legal and ethical use terms above still apply. Test without
keeping plaintext with:

```sh
./unfairplay verify --input AnotherApp.ipa
```

The decryption path handles ARMv6/Thumb-1, ARMv7, ARM64, and
ARM64_32/watchOS slices.
Available pre-encryption page hashes must match; a mismatch fails closed.
Older executables without these tables can decrypt, but report
`plaintext_verified=false`.

### Convert an IPA for macOS

This requires an encrypted IPA personalized for the same Store enrollment as
your saved model. Convert it with:

```sh
./unfairplay convert-ipa-macos \
  --input App.ipa \
  --model /private/path/fairplay-enrollment.bin
```

Omit `--model` to use the saved model. The default output is `App.macos.ipa`.
Use `--output` to choose another path or `--force` to replace an existing
output.

The command uses a saved version-2 enrollment model. You can instead use a
matching private 16-byte credential:

```sh
chmod 600 credential.bin
./unfairplay convert-ipa-macos \
  --input App.ipa \
  --credential credential.bin
```

The conversion:

- decodes the current private record with the direct enrollment model;
- validates and rewrites the personalized SINF into the macOS layout;
- preserves its app key, signature, rights, and other private fields;
- adds every SINF copy declared by Apple for encrypted frameworks and
  extensions; and
- leaves all Mach-O executables byte-identical and encrypted.

Model-based conversion supports the observed 440- and 448-byte private SINF
records and the same bounded appended-rights geometry used by recovery.

The result is still an IPA, not a macOS installer. A macOS iOS-app wrapper or
compatible installer must preserve this basic layout:

```text
App iOS.app/
  WrappedBundle -> Wrapper/App.app
  Wrapper/App.app
  Wrapper/iTunesMetadata.plist
```

The converted IPA and wrapper contain a private account license. Keep them
private. This feature does not decrypt, modify, re-sign, or bypass checks inside
the app. Apps may still reject macOS, require unavailable hardware, or depend on
services that are not present on macOS.

## Advanced commands

`collect` and `recover` expose the two setup stages for diagnostics and
archived captures. `doctor` checks a capture, IPA, or model.

```sh
sudo ./unfairplay collect --app /Applications/App.app --ipa App.ipa --output App.capture
./unfairplay recover --capture App.capture --output App.recovery
```

## FAQ

### What is an enrollment?

An enrollment is the FairPlay state created when an Apple Account uses the Mac
App Store on a Mac. It links the account, Mac, and FairPlay selector. `setup`
turns that state into a reusable private model.

### What are SINF, SUPF, SIDB, and SC Info?

# 网易云音乐 · MyGo

用 Go 和 [MyGo](https://github.com/egoist/mygo) 写的第三方网易云音乐桌面客户端，原生界面，无 WebView。

## 功能

- 扫码登录，登录态保存在系统凭据存储中
- 每日推荐、推荐歌单、排行榜、我的歌单
- 搜索单曲、歌手、专辑、用户与播客，输入时显示搜索建议，保留搜索历史
- 歌手页的热门与最新歌曲、专辑与动态，关注歌手；专辑页与用户页
- 播客：浏览与收听节目，订阅播客；在本机把节目转写成字幕（Qwen3-ASR），像歌词一样随播放滚动
- 私人 FM（推荐 / 熟悉 / 探索）与心动模式
- 边下边播，支持标准 / 较高 / 极高 / 无损（FLAC）/ Hi-Res 音质
- 听过的歌曲缓存在本机，再次播放无需等待
- 音量均衡，暂停与继续时淡出淡入，拖动进度无杂音
- 退出后再打开，从上次的播放队列与进度继续
- 逐字歌词与翻译，正在播放页的「律动」视图与歌曲评论
- 刘海播放器：在屏幕顶部刘海处显示迷你播放器，悬停展开（在设置中开启）
- 喜欢歌曲、播放队列、随机与循环播放
- 浅色 / 深色 / 跟随系统

## 构建

需要 Go 1.27+。

```bash
go tool mygo dev     # 开发模式运行
go tool mygo build   # 打包到 build/
go test ./...        # 运行测试
```

## 致谢

- [MyGo](https://github.com/egoist/mygo)：原生 UI 与应用框架
- [NeteaseCloudMusicApi](https://github.com/Binaryify/NeteaseCloudMusicApi)：eapi 加密与登录流程的参考
- [folia-major](https://github.com/chthollyphile/folia-major)：歌词动画效果的参考
- [sherpa-onnx](https://github.com/k2-fsa/sherpa-onnx)、[Qwen3-ASR](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-ASR) 与 [Silero VAD](https://github.com/snakers4/silero-vad)：本机语音识别

本项目与网易云音乐官方无关，音乐版权归各权利人所有。

UNCUT

The lossless, headless coding agent harness.

One 7 MB static binary, four tools, plain stdin/stdout.
No TUI. No telemetry. No silent context cuts.

Linux · macOS · Windows · amd64 + arm64 · MIT

Landing page: balanov.pro/uncut

[![CI](https://github.com/Balanov/uncut/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/Balanov/uncut/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/Balanov/uncut)](https://github.com/Balanov/uncut/releases/latest) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-green.svg)](LICENSE) [![Go](https://img.shields.io/badge/Go-1.26%2B-00ADD8?logo=go&logoColor=white)](go.mod) UNCUT is a tiny coding-agent harness for shell pipelines, CI jobs, containers, and agent experiments. It deliberately has no TUI, telemetry, plugin system, background agents, automatic retries, or context compaction. The entire conversation is sent on every model call. File contents and combined command output are never truncated by UNCUT. If the provider cuts a response at its output limit, UNCUT exits with an error instead of presenting a partial answer as success. content.readme:
The open-source helpdesk.

Features · How it works · Quick start · Self-hosting · Docs · Community · Support

⭐ Help more teams find opendesk. Star this repo!

## opendesk opendesk brings your support email, live chat and help center into one shared inbox, and every change shows up live for everyone on the team. It ships as a hosted service at [opendesk.sh](https://opendesk.sh) and as a self-hosted install, and **the two run the same code**. Ollie, the built-in AI, drafts, triages and answers alongside your team, with any Anthropic or OpenAI-compatible provider, including local models. ## Features - **Shared inbox** - tickets with status, priority, assignee, team, tags and SLA; notes, merge, snooze, bulk edit - **Mailboxes** - forward your support address in, reply from it through Google, Microsoft or SMTP - **Live chat** - an embeddable widget with identity verification, typing and live delivery - **Knowledge base** - collections and articles, published to a public help center - **Ollie and bots** - drafts, summaries, triage, translation and chat answers from your knowledge base - **Automations and SLAs** - rules that run on ticket events, and targets per priority - **Reports and CSAT** - volume, response and resolution times, breaches and satisfaction - **Integrations** - Linear, GitHub, Jira, Sentry, Slack, Stripe and any MCP server - **Public API** - the REST API the app itself uses, plus signed webhooks, a realtime socket and MCP - **Apps** - desktop for macOS, Windows and Linux, and a native iPhone app ## How it works opendesk is one Go binary (the API, background jobs and the event relay), an Elixir realtime gateway that holds no database connection, and Postgres. Every change that someone else should see is written as an event in the same transaction as the change; the relay publishes it to NATS, the gateway pushes it to browsers, and webhooks deliver it to your endpoints. There is no Redis and no Kafka. ```mermaid flowchart LR B["Browsers · apps"] --> C["Caddy"] C -- "/socket" --> RT["Realtime gateway"] C --> OD["opendesk
API · jobs · web app"] OD --> DB[("Postgres")] OD -- "events" --> N{{"NATS"}} N --> RT OD --> WH["Webhooks"] OD --> M["Google · Microsoft · SMTP"] ``` Self-hosted, NATS runs embedded in the opendesk binary and the whole stack sits behind Caddy on one domain. The hosted service splits the same binary into API and worker roles. Full write-up in the [introduction](https://docs.opendesk.sh/getting-started/introduction/) and the [cloud architecture](https://docs.opendesk.sh/cloud/architecture/). ## Quick start You need Go, Node.js with pnpm, Elixir, and Docker for Postgres. ```bash git clone https://github.com/useopendesk/opendesk && cd opendesk cp .env.example .env make dev-db # Postgres on localhost:55432 make api # the Go API and workers, with embedded NATS on :4222 make realtime # the Elixir gateway on :4000 make web # the web app on :5173 ``` Open `http://localhost:5173` and sign up. Until you configure a mail driver, verification and invitation emails are printed to the API log. `make site` and `make docs` run the marketing site and the docs. content.readme:
A tiny, local-first AI harness for people who prefer a terminal.
One static binary. Zero dependencies. No TUI. No telemetry. MIT.

## Why Shim? Model-agnostic coding agents are everywhere. Setting them up is still too hard: provider IDs, API endpoints, MCP JSON, skills directories, and a new interface for every tool. **Shim is the small adapter between you and all of that.** - **Talk or type commands.** A full scriptable CLI for experts; ordinary language for everyone else. - **Use a local mini-model as the command router.** It translates management requests into an allowlisted command. Mutating commands require confirmation. - **Bring any model API.** Native OpenAI-compatible and Anthropic adapters, plus presets for popular hosted and local providers. - **Bring any MCP server or Agent Skill.** MCP over stdio and Streamable HTTP; lazy `SKILL.md` loading from common directories. - **Stay light.** No Electron, Node, Python, Docker, database, background daemon, or UI framework. - **Own your state.** Plain JSON config and JSONL sessions. API keys come from environment variables and are never written to Shim's config. Measured on the maintainer's Windows machine for v0.1.0: **7.29 MiB** stripped binary and **9.96 ms median** process startup for `shim --version` over 30 runs. This is a local measurement, not a cross-platform performance guarantee. ## Install ### Download Get a static binary for Windows, macOS, or Linux from [Releases](https://github.com/Balanov/shim/releases), put it on your `PATH`, then run: ```sh shim setup shim ``` On PowerShell, use `.\shim.exe` when running the binary from the current directory. ### With Go Go 1.25+: ```sh go install github.com/Balanov/shim/cmd/shim@v0.1.0 shim setup ``` ### From source ```sh git clone https://github.com/Balanov/shim.git cd shim go test ./... go build -trimpath -ldflags="-s -w" -o shim ./cmd/shim ./shim setup ``` Windows also has `scripts/build.ps1`; Unix has `scripts/build.sh`. ## Two ways to use it ### Just talk ```text you › найди локальные модели ↳ /discover --add Run this command? [y/N] y you › show my tools ↳ /tools you › fix the failing tests in this repository ``` Shim has deterministic offline phrases for common English and Russian management commands. For other languages, assign a local model as the router: ```sh shim router use ollama/qwen3:4b ``` The router sees non-command chat text so it can distinguish configuration requests from agent tasks. Use a loopback model if you want that step to stay on your machine. **No model weights are bundled or silently downloaded**; that would defeat the tiny-binary goal. Your primary model handles ordinary conversation in whatever language it supports. ### Use the complete CLI ```sh # Local models: discover and configure all running servers shim model discover --add # Hosted models shim model add openrouter anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5 --name claude --use shim model add openai gpt-5 --name gpt --use shim model add huggingface org/model --name hf --use # Any OpenAI-compatible endpoint shim model add custom my-model --name mine \ --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1 --use # One-shot agent run shim run --read-only "explain this repository" shim run --yes --verbose "fix the tests and verify the result" # Interactive terminal shim ``` Run `shim help` for the full command surface. ## Model providers | Preset | Adapter | Credential environment variable | |---|---|---| | `ollama` | OpenAI-compatible | None | | `lmstudio` | OpenAI-compatible | None | | `llamacpp` | OpenAI-compatible | None | | `openai` | OpenAI-compatible | `OPENAI_API_KEY` | | `openrouter` | OpenAI-compatible | `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` | | `anthropic` | Anthropic Messages | `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | | `gemini` | Gemini OpenAI-compatible endpoint | `GEMINI_API_KEY` | | `github` | GitHub Models | `GITHUB_TOKEN` | | `huggingface` | Hugging Face router | `HF_TOKEN` | | `custom` | OpenAI-compatible or Anthropic | Optional, configurable | “Any model” means any model exposed through a supported HTTP API. GGUF and other local weights run through Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp, or another compatible inference server; Shim is the harness, not an inference engine. PowerShell example: ```powershell $env:OPENROUTER_API_KEY = "..." shim model add openrouter your/model --name main --use shim model test main ``` For persist

content.readme: # diff-tour Walk through a diff the way a senior engineer reads it. **English** | [日本語](README.ja.md) [![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/init-co-jp/diff-tour)](https://github.com/init-co-jp/diff-tour/releases) [![CI](https://github.com/init-co-jp/diff-tour/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/init-co-jp/diff-tour/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue)](LICENSE) ![tour walking through a change that adds coupons](demo/demo-en.gif) A tour of a branch that adds coupons: what the change is for, how the usage limit is enforced, a question to think about, and the answer: applying a coupon twice to one order uses it up twice. > [!NOTE] > diff-tour is growing fast. The tour format and the screens may still change from release to release. ## Quick start You need git and one of [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code), [Codex CLI](https://github.com/openai/codex), [Gemini CLI](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli), [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) 2, [Copilot CLI](https://github.com/github/copilot-cli) or [Pi](https://pi.dev), signed in. ```sh curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/init-co-jp/diff-tour/main/install.sh | sh cd your-repo tour ``` Then it goes like this: 1. **Setup** (first time only): choose the display language and the LLM that writes the tour. Both have a recommended choice selected, so press Enter twice. 2. **Pick a change**: the changes you can tour are listed, with your current branch selected. Press Enter. 3. **Writing**: the LLM writes the tour. This takes 2 to 5 minutes. 4. **The tour**: **→** goes forward, **←** goes back, **q** quits. If `tour` is not found, add the line the install script printed to your shell profile. To see a finished tour first, with no LLM and no sign-in, play the one from the GIF. It opens at once: ```sh git clone https://github.com/init-co-jp/diff-tour-example && cd diff-tour-example curl -fsSLO https://raw.githubusercontent.com/init-co-jp/diff-tour/main/tours/example-coupons.en.json tour example-coupons.en.json ``` Other ways to install are in [Install](#install), and an example repository to try is in [First run](#first-run). ## What it is AI can write code that works. It does not teach you *why* the code is written that way, or what a reviewer would worry about. `tour` turns a git change into a guided tour you step through with two keys, **→** and **←**. The tour shows what a senior engineer looks at when they read the change: - **How they read it.** What the change is for, where to spend time, and which files to jump to next, including files that did not change. - **What they ask.** Does it keep the promises the old code kept? What happens when something fails, or runs twice? Can it be rolled out and rolled back safely? Who can call it, and with what input? What happens at 100 times the data? Is the next change easier or harder? Would the tests fail if the code broke? - **How they judge.** Which findings must be fixed and which are only suggestions or nits, what looks risky but is fine and why, what is done well, and whether the change makes the codebase better overall. - **Where they stop and say "wait".** These come as questions, so you can predict the answer before you see it. This view comes from what experienced engineers have written down about reading and reviewing code, collected in [`internal/generate/lessons`](internal/generate/lessons) (in Japanese). The LLM reads it before every tour. The tour is written by an LLM you already use: Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Copilot CLI or Pi. `tour` is read-only. It never changes your files or your repository. ## How it works ```text your repository cache directory (deleted after writing) ─────────────── ────────────────────────────────────── git archive ──────────────────▶ base/ files before the change git archive ──────────────────▶ head/ files after the change git diff ──────────────────▶ change.diff git log ──────────────────▶ commits.txt (built into tour) ──────────────────▶ lessons/ what senior engineers have learned │ ▼ Claude Code / Codex / Gemini / OpenCode / Copilot / Pi, started in that directory with read-only permissions. It reads, then writes the tour as JSON. │ ▼ tour checks every file and line the JSON points to. If something is wrong, it asks the LLM to fix only that (up to 2 times). The tour is saved. │

# Open Screen Sharing

![Open Screen Sharing on iPad connected to macOS and vphone-cli](assets/readme/hero.png)

Open Screen Sharing aims to develop superior servers and clients based on the private protocol used by Apple VNC (macOS's Screen Sharing server and ScreenSharing.app).

## Installation

### iOS

[![Download on the App Store](assets/readme/app-store-badge.svg)](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/open-screen-sharing/id6818992574)

The App Store version is **\$1 through October 31, 2026**, then **\$2**. Your purchase supports my work.

The App Store version excludes the following features due to App Store restrictions:

* **Apple VNC server:** relies on background keep-alive mechanisms and a lockdown exploit.
* **Dragging files directly from a remote Mac into other iOS/iPadOS apps:** relies on a private API.

To use these features, sideload the app by adding the source to SideStore or AltStore:

```
https://github.com/nekohasekai/open-screen-sharing/releases/latest/download/altstore.json
```

Or download [OpenScreenSharing.ipa](https://github.com/nekohasekai/open-screen-sharing/releases/latest/download/OpenScreenSharing.ipa) and sideload it.

### macOS

Download and install [OpenScreenSharing.pkg](https://github.com/nekohasekai/open-screen-sharing/releases/latest/download/OpenScreenSharing.pkg).

### Nightly builds

You can download and install nightly builds from the [Nightly release](https://github.com/nekohasekai/open-screen-sharing/releases/tag/nightly). For AltStore or SideStore on iOS, the source URL is:

```
https://github.com/nekohasekai/open-screen-sharing/releases/download/nightly/altstore.json
```

You can also switch to the Nightly track in the App settings of the macOS app and update directly.

## Features

1. Compared to the original ScreenSharing.app:

* Optimized for local networks
* Optimized for public networks (runs smoothly with Tailscale P2P)
* Fixed language switching
* Exclusive mouse support
* Debug HUD support
* Interactions optimized for iOS and iPadOS

2. Apple VNC server implementation on iOS and iPadOS

* Requires iOS 27 (Xcode DeviceHub); no jailbreak or TrollStore required (though sideloading is obviously necessary)

**Decision model.** Jev (TypeSafe) answers a typed question about a turn with a calibrated probability in under half a second. Judged reads: search, file and log reads return what counts. Per-turn toolbox: only the tools the turn needs are sent. Stall detection: a turn that stops making progress ends. 44 paired runs, decisions off and on: 22 of 22 passed each way; a codebase question 54,661 to 14,367 input tokens (−74%); an edit with a test and ten one-file fixes read the same files either way (within ±11%) ([`docs/features/DECIDE.md`](docs/features/DECIDE.md)). **Workflows, the deterministic harness.** Say the steps; the coder writes one YAML per step. [`mario`](https://github.com/guregodevo/mario) runs the graph. Independent steps run in parallel. A step is done when its check passes. A gate waits for approval with the diff. A failed run resumes at the failed step. Started by hand, from CI or on local cron ([`docs/features/WORKFLOWS.md`](docs/features/WORKFLOWS.md)).
